chapter: Changing styles, the road and nightlife
title: Loss of regional differences and the roughness of early jazz
summary: DeMichael laments homogenisation; Saunders loves jazz's crude roots and says dressing it up changes it.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Well, there's been a decline of differences in this country, I think, ever since -- I guess, during the war is when it started. And mass media accents are disappearing. Regional styles of cooking are disappearing. And in music, it's the same thing.
And you could tell a guy was from Texas by the way that he played.
And it's the same way with the bands. we're given this blanket of high-quality anonymity.
That is unfortunate. I'd rather have the roughness --

Oh, this is -- I always loved that, I always loved that -- you said it, roughness, the crude style of jazz, if you want to name it that. But this is what I -- I mean, I think this is where jazz comes from. And these are the roots of jazz.
Right, right. But when you take it and you dress it up and put fancy clothes on it and all of that, it just doesn't come out the same.
